case_title: State of Orissa v. Khaga @ Khageswar Naik & Ors.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Modified conviction to s.304 Part II IPC and sentenced to 8 years RI
neutral_facts: The accused entered the room of the victim's daughter at midnight, molested her, and then confronted the victim. The victim, an elderly man, abused the accused verbally. In response, two of the accused retrieved weapons and attacked the victim, resulting in his death. The victim's body was found the following day. The prosecution alleged that the accused committed offenses under multiple sections of the IPC, including murder. The trial court convicted the accused of murder and sentenced them to life imprisonment. The High Court, however, modified the conviction to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under s.304 Part II IPC and sentenced them to 8 years of rigorous imprisonment. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, restoring the trial court's conviction for murder.
